metadata.note: The Northern Railroad of New York / Ogdensburg and Lake Champlain, Ogdensburg - Rouses Point (117 mi), 1850-1953. One traced geometry drawn by eight features, split at each change of the company that ran the trains (CLAUDE.md Rule 4): Northern RR of NY 1850-1864; O&LC 1865-1869; Vermont Central (lessee) 1870-1872; Central Vermont (lessee) 1873-1876; O&LC 1877-1885; Central Vermont (second lease) 1886-1895; O&LC 1896-1900; Rutland (Ogdensburg Division) 1901-1953.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn: (a) the Rouses Point - Alburgh, VT tail (3.6 mi) that Rutland trains used 1901-1953 over the CV lake bridge - it belongs to a future Rutland Island Line feature; (b) the O&LC 'Lamoille Valley Extension' Rouses Point - Maquam (built 1883, service ended July 1884) - no confirmable passenger year, route and operator unsettled; (c) freight-only service 1953-1961 and the surviving Norwood - Ogdensburg freight track (Rule 1).
not_yet_sourced: Passenger evidence 1877-1950 is thin: firm anchors are 1851, 1865, 1875, 1951 and 1953; every era between 1875 and 1951 is drawn on continuity. One Official Guide / Appletons / CV / Rutland timetable each from the 1880s, 1890s and 1920s-30s would source three NOT SOURCED eras.

Second Central Vermont lease start: June 1884 (Wikipedia Rouses Point station, uncited 'regained control'), 1885 (derivative web page) or 1886 (Worthen, 'another C. V. RR. lease in 1886'). Split drawn at 1886; move to 1884 if the 1884 event was a lease or operating agreement.

Rutland takeover 1899 vs 1901: RRHS history 'purchased the OLC in 1899'; ICC valuation (via nashuacitystation.org) O&LC Railway 'merges with Rutland Railroad Company' Feb 1 1899; RRHS timeline consolidation Oct 26-28 1901; american-rails Sept 27 1901. Drawn O&LC to 1900, Rutland from 1901; move to 1899 if a timetable of 1899-1900 prints the line as a Rutland division.

1858 'Ogdensburg Railroad Company': scripophily.net has the Northern RR reorganized Jan 6 1858 under that name after the 1856 foreclosure sale (U.S. Reports 79:384); Doherty has the Northern company existing until 1864. If the 1858 company was a separate operating corporation, Rule 4 would want a further split (Northern RR 1850-1857 / Ogdensburg RR 1858-1864). Not split - the only source is a certificate dealer's summary.

The research queue's '1850-1913' end year is spurious: no 1913 event exists on this road (the O&LC ceased to exist in 1901); 1913 is the NYC consolidation year of the neighbouring Rome, Watertown and Ogdensburg queue entry, probably copied across by mistake. Not used.

1896 vs 1898 end of the second CV lease: 1896 used (Worthen, Wikipedia O&LC and Rouses Point station); Wikipedia's Central Vermont article says 1898, probably the O&LC's Dec 1 1898 reorganization. The exact 1896 day is not established.
[1]/[2] split year: drawn at the Aug 1 1865 conveyance rather than the June 1864 incorporation of the O&LC.

headway_min is an estimate in every segment except 1951-1953 (Feb 1952 Official Guide); the 19th-century value is carried from the single Sept 1865 timetable. avg_speed_kmh is derived from the 1865 advertisement (39) and the 1951 Guide (32); no other year measured.
When the line went from regular passenger trains to mixed-only service, and whether the Rutland ran Ogdensburg - Boston / Montreal through cars 1900-1950, is not researched.

Of the routed length 116.5 mi runs on ways tagged old_railway_operator=Rutland and 0.2 mi on untagged rail; no straight-line legs. Norwood - Ogdensburg is the surviving New York & Ogdensburg (ex-Rutland) track; Norwood - Rouses Point (lifted 1964) is the abandoned grade as mapped in OSM. Every waypoint lies within 1.6 km of the line except Bangor (4.3 km: the OSM place node is the Bangor hamlet south of the line; the station was at North Bangor). Ends: the Ogdensburg end is where the OSM Rutland-tagged track ends at the harbour; the Rouses Point end is in the village just east of the D&H crossing, BEFORE the trestle/fill to the CV lake bridge, so the Rutland's 1901 gauntlet connection is not drawn and the pre-1901 features do not run onto it. Later-alignment caveat: one geometry serves all eras 1850-1953; no main-line relocation is known, but the exact 1850s terminal arrangements at Ogdensburg (harbour) and Rouses Point (wharf) are not verified against period maps, and the Ogdensburg end follows the modern OSM track. The Rouses Point - Alburgh tail (3.6 mi) used by Rutland trains 1901-1953 is deliberately not drawn here (belongs to a Rutland Island Line feature).

segments.note: Opened for traffic Sept 20 1850 (RRHS timeline); construction reached Rouses Point Oct 1 1850 (Wikipedia). First passenger-specific evidence is 1851: Fowler's NY file letters stations from the 1851 Dinsmore Guide. Doherty (RLHS 1938, via the Lincoln Papers) credits the road with no passenger killed or injured in its first eleven years, i.e. carrying passengers 1850-1861; 1862-1864 rests on continuity to the Sept 1865 timetable, with no suspension recorded. Route: Ogdensburg - Lisbon - Madrid - Norwood - Winthrop - North Lawrence - Moira - Brushton - Bangor - Malone - Burke - Chateaugay - Churubusco - Ellenburgh - Altona - Mooers Forks - Mooers - Champlain - Rouses Point. In 1851-57 the favoured summer route Montreal - Rouses Point - Ogdensburg - St. Lawrence steamers (Worthen). Trains ended at Rouses Point; the lake crossing to Alburgh was Vermont & Canada property, not drawn. Trustees for the second-mortgage bondholders from c.1854, foreclosure sale 1856 and a possible reorganization as the Ogdensburg Railroad Co. on Jan 6 1858 are treated as one continuing operator (see not_yet_sourced). Era ends when the Ogdensburg and Lake Champlain took the property (Aug 1 1865; that company was incorporated June 18 1864 - the split here follows the conveyance). headway_min is an ESTIMATE carried from the Sept 1865 timetable (three trains each way daily, Sundays excepted); no timetable of these years was read for frequency.
sources: Segment-level: opening year from the RRHS timeline and Wikipedia; passenger stations from the 1851 Dinsmore Guide (Fowler NY SL201 s.29); 1850-1861 passenger carriage from Doherty via the Lincoln Papers; 1862-1864 by continuity.

Era ends with the lease to the Vermont Central, March 1 1870.

segments.note: Returned to the O&LC April 1 1877 (Worthen). The O&LC tried for a Great Lakes - Portland route of its own via the Portland & Ogdensburg, building the 'Lamoille Valley Extension' east from Rouses Point in 1883 (not drawn - no confirmable passenger year). A NY act of June 29 1882 (ch. 364) regulating 'freight and passenger' interchange with the CV at Rouses Point assumes a passenger business. SOURCE CONFLICT on the end: CV 'regained control' June 1884 (Wikipedia, uncited), CV lease 1885 (derivative web page), 'another C. V. RR. lease in 1886' (Worthen, in print). Split at 1886 because only Worthen names and dates a lease; 1884 'control' may have been stock control. No timetable of 1877-1885 was read - drawn on continuity. headway_min is an ESTIMATE carried from the Sept 1865 timetable (three trains each way daily, Sundays excepted); no timetable of these years was read for frequency.

segments.note: The O&LC ran its own trains again after the CV receivership of 1896; it bought three Schenectady locomotives in 1897 (american-rails.com; later Rutland 10-12). Reorganized Dec 1 1898 as the Ogdensburg and Lake Champlain RAILWAY Co. (ICC) - same road, not a split. The Rutland's role 1899-1901 is unsettled: RRHS says it 'purchased the OLC in 1899', the ICC valuation has the O&LC Railway merging with the Rutland Feb 1 1899, while the RRHS timeline dates the consolidation Oct 26-28 1901. Drawn as O&LC to 1900, Rutland from 1901, matching the Rutland layer's treatment of the Bennington & Rutland. No passenger timetable of 1896-1900 was read - continuity. headway_min is an ESTIMATE carried from the Sept 1865 timetable (three trains each way daily, Sundays excepted); no timetable of these years was read for frequency.

segments.note: Consolidated into the Rutland Railroad Oct 26-28 1901 (RRHS timeline) and run as its Ogdensburg Division. NYC stock control 1904-05 and the New Haven's half-share from 1911 (both out by 1941) were stock only - the trains stayed Rutland trains; Rutland Railroad became the Rutland Railway on Nov 1 1950 (reorganization, not a split). Trains ran beyond Rouses Point to Alburgh, VT over the Island Line / CV lake-bridge track, which this feature does not draw. No Rutland timetable of 1901-1950 was read for this line, and nothing dates the change from regular passenger trains to the mixed-only service of 1951 - drawn on continuity to the 1951 Guide. headway_min 720 (two trains each way) is an ESTIMATE, not from a timetable.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: the 1901 start is the RRHS consolidation date, but no passenger timetable of 1901-1950 was checked for this line; frequency is an estimate.

segments.note: Official Guide Feb 1952, Rutland Table 4 'Ogdensburg Division' (schedules of Sept 30 1951), read directly: No. 7, labelled Mixed, Alburgh 12.00 noon, Rouses Point 12.14, Lisbon 6.35 pm; one mixed train each way daily (headway 1440 from that table). Station index lists Altona, Burke, Champlain, Chateaugay, Ellenburgh, Lisbon, Moira and Mooers as passenger stations. A mixed train counts as passenger service (Rule 1). All Rutland passenger service ended with the strike of June 26 1953 (RRHS timeline) and the Ogdensburg mixed did not resume. Freight continued to Sept 25 1961; Rouses Point - Norwood was lifted 1964; Norwood - Ogdensburg survives as freight-only New York & Ogdensburg track - none of that is drawn.
sources: Segment-level: 1951 service from the Feb 1952 Official Guide Rutland Table 4 (read directly); 1953 end from the RRHS timeline (June 26 1953 strike, all passenger service eliminated).
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (schedules of Sept 30 1951), Rutland Table 4 'Ogdensburg Division' and station index (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt)
